rejection_note: Dropped by the authors on 2026-09-28 for exceeding the compute budget: reconstruction gives a 51-package environment on Python 3.7, and 8 of the 9 AURA arms hit the 6-hour limit per arm. Where each arm stopped depended on its node's install speed (79-169 s per probe), not on the method, so the arms cannot be compared head to head. Decided on runtime alone, the same for every arm.

name: rllib
validation_notes: The project's own test file, unmodified: one test, which trains a tabular Q-learning agent on gym's Taxi-v3 at import time and asserts the mean reward of the last ten episodes is exactly 8.0. Added on the authors' request without local screening -- torch is too heavy for the laptop -- so the baseline and pip_upgrade arms on the cluster are its screen.
rejection_note: Dropped by the authors on 2026-10-02: on the cluster neither the declared baseline nor its reconstruction produced a working environment, so no arm can start. Not screened locally (torch is too heavy for the laptop).

name: slicelabeler
validation_notes: The project's own pytest suite, unmodified: all 59 tests pass at baseline in about 15 seconds, against Flask's test client, SQLite and a fake filesystem (pyfakefs); no service is needed. A Flask app for labelling medical-image slices with a fully frozen 18-package set: Flask 1.1.2, Werkzeug 0.16.1, Jinja2 2.11.3, itsdangerous 1.1.0, Click 7.0, Flask-SQLAlchemy 2.4.1 and SQLAlchemy 1.3.19, with numpy, nibabel and Pillow. Upgrading everything naively fails at collection with sqlalchemy.orm.exc.MappedAnnotationError: SQLAlchemy 2 reads the models' annotations differently -- a runtime coupling no package metadata declares. A keep, chosen for the coupled-major-upgrade stratum by that structural criterion, not by any AURA result. Does not declare pytest; the runner is installed by environment_setup. On the cluster some upgraded combinations -- pyfakefs 5.10 with nibabel 4.0 was seen -- make the suite spin at full CPU instead of failing; every such probe held its slot for the default hour. The test timeout is therefore 60 s for this subject, four times the suite's normal 7-15 s, and applies to every arm alike: a combination that has not finished its tests in a minute is rejected as failing.
rejection_note: Dropped by the authors on 2026-10-01: the oracle is not deterministic under the harness. Of 79 test runs across its arms, about 70 finished in 0.25-21 s and 8 hung until the timeout, with none in between -- and the unmodified baseline pins passed in about 8 s in five arms but hung in greedy's, twice (once for the full hour). A hang is read as failing, so roughly one probe in ten was rejected regardless of the versions it tested. Neither the NFS checkout (since moved to local disk) nor the one-thread limits explain it; the cause, somewhere in its pyfakefs suite under the harness, was not diagnosed.
